claim: Prediction robustness and explanation robustness are distinct properties.
support: MLP keeps high class stability while showing materially lower Jaccard and higher normalized L1 than LIN across all tasks.
caution: Do not infer explanation robustness from prediction stability.

claim: LIN_SGD_LOGISTIC provides the most stable SHAP explanations across all three tasks.
support: LIN has the highest Jaccard@5/@10 and Spearman and the lowest normalized L1 in CIC34, TON10 and TON2.
caution: Limited to the frozen PF1 perturbation protocol and SHAP configuration.

claim: HGB explanations can remain stable while HGB predictions are comparatively perturbation-sensitive.
support: CIC34 and TON10 HGB have lower prediction stability than LIN/MLP while keeping high explanation-overlap metrics.
caution: Report prediction and explanation robustness separately.

claim: Increasing perturbation intensity generally degrades robustness, but the response is model-dependent.
support: 39/45 task-family-metric contrasts have the same 0.10 vs 0.01 direction in all five seeds; exceptions concentrate mainly in MLP overlap/rank metrics.
caution: Do not claim strict monotonicity for every metric.

claim: Robustness is heterogeneous across predicted-class strata in multiclass tasks.
support: At intensity 0.10, prediction-stability ranges are large for CIC34/HGB and TON10/HGB.
caution: These are predicted-class strata, not ground-truth class error rates.

claim: The perturbed source feature materially affects robustness.
support: Feature-level stability varies strongly, especially for HGB; CIC34 Tot sum/Max/Rate and TON src_ip_bytes are among sensitive perturbations.
caution: Interpret within the frozen perturbation generator.

claim: Top-k ablation response is not guaranteed to be monotonic in k.
support: TON2/LIN prediction-change rate falls from ~0.491 at Top-5 to ~0.201 at Top-10 in all five seeds.
caution: Treat as functional masking response, not causal importance.

claim: Canonical duplicate profiles do not drive the main conclusions.
support: Unique-profile weighting changes principal pooled metrics only marginally; largest absolute delta is ~0.0031.
caution: Canonical weighting remains primary by protocol.
